title.narrative: 'Calzada del Agua'; An innovative solution for sustainable water management in Mexican cities

description.narrative: The main goal of this feasibility project was to visualise the technical and economic feasibility of the implementation of the Bluebloqs system at Mercado de la Merced in Oaxaca de Juarez and to make a decision with regard to the realization of a pilot project.The results indicate that the implementation of the Urban Water buffer project at the market is technically and institutionally feasible. In addition, an Urban Water buffer appears to be both a sustainable solution to the problem of flooding in the city and a reliable local source of water for the 300 users of the market. In addition, the Urban Water buffer could make a significant contribution to improving the spatial quality of the Calzada de la República and of the city.Based on the findings of the feasibility study, the implementation of a demonstration project is recommended as an important next step for the development of this new technology in Oaxaca and the rest of Mexico. The demonstration of the solution will help to remove uncertainties – regarding the capacity of the subsurface for water storage and aspects related to water quality – among local stakeholders. To facilitate decision-making for the implementation of the Urban Water buffer demonstration project, a preliminary design, an associated cost estimate and an implementation plan have been developed.The possibilities for applying for and granting the necessary permits have been discussed with the National Water Commission "CONAGUA", whereby the representatives have a positive attitude towards granting the relevant permits for a possible pilot project. As a result, concrete agreements have been made with the Municipality of Oaxaca about co-financing the follow-up process.In conclusion, the Urban Water buffer concept offers a circular solution to current and future urban water management challenges in Oaxaca, and can become a reference for circular water management in other cities in Mexico and even in the first example in LATAM.By implementing a pilot, the opportunities for upscaling can be evaluated based on empirical data on the impact and efficiency of the Urban Water buffer concept in the Mexican climatic, geological and institutional context.
